audience: a parent or patient-group leader without medical training

sentences.text: Krabbe disease is linked to the gene GALC in curated databases, and no contradicting evidence is recorded [e_3dbc42738b5a].
A low level of tissue galactocerebrosidase activity is an observed feature of Krabbe disease in the databases [e_371301408104].
GALC and a second gene called PSAP both take part in the same curated pathway, glycosphingolipid catabolism [e_993c3f6ead03] [e_8f8f3574e614].
Constellate also links Krabbe disease to PSAP, but this link is only inferred from the infantile subtype, with confidence 0.475 (lowest subtype confidence times 0.5) [e_2c5236d2f740].
That PSAP link holds for the named subtype and not necessarily for every form of Krabbe disease [e_2c5236d2f740].
Krabbe disease and metachromatic leukodystrophy look similar in their listed symptoms, but this is a computed score (simGIC 0.216) and not a diagnosis [e_e270315fe572].
The two clinical trials in this set are about metachromatic leukodystrophy, not Krabbe disease, and both are listed as not yet recruiting [e_c9e7007213ce] [e_82dda6df3b0d].
These edges do not show any trial for Krabbe disease itself, so they say nothing about what can help [e_c9e7007213ce].
